title: introduce-credential-routers-and-client-side-backpressure-adapters
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers reported intermittent token swap latency and client-side queueing spikes under high-throughput streaming workloads. Motivation: give SDKs a lightweight policy layer to route credential providers at call time and a small, opinionated backpressure adapter to prevent unbounded memory growth in long-lived pull/push streams. This PR introduces two orthogonal pieces: 1) CredentialRouter: a configurable router that maps request metadata (route, model, region, priority) to a credential provider chain. Router supports simple rules (prefix, exact, regex) and a fallback cascade so apps can express per-route ephemeral credentials without central orchestration. 2) BackpressureAdapter: a client-side stream operator for pull/push streaming that applies a bounded in-memory window, optional drop/slowdown policies, and a token-bucket throttler for outgoing requests to avoid overfilling the runtime queue. The changeset touches TypeScript/Go/Python SDKs and the redwood runtime test fixtures to validate multi-SDK interoperability. Key goals: - preserve existing public APIs where possible and add opt-in constructors - provide clear telemetry hooks (events emitted when router changes provider or when adapter drops/throttles) - ship pragmatic defaults that work for common server-side SLOs Checklist: [x] Spec and API doc in PR description [x] TypeScript implementation and tests [x] Python wrapper and tests [x] Go implementation and tests [x] Integration test against local runtime fixture [x] Docs and changelog entry Major user-facing notes: - Default behavior is opt-in; no change to existing credential lookup semantics unless app constructs a CredentialRouter. - BackpressureAdapter defaults to a 100-message window with drop-oldest behavior; configurable via constructor. - Added minor SDK version bumps: ts-sdk -> v1.31.0, py-sdk -> v1.22.3, go-sdk -> v1.9.7. Migration notes included in release_notes below.
commit_summary: feat(cred): add CredentialRouter core and rule engine
feat(stream): add BackpressureAdapter with token-bucket and drop/slow strategies
chore(py): expose router bindings in Python SDK and add integration tests
chore(go): implement router and adapter; add unit tests and examples
docs: add usage examples and migration notes to SDK changelogs
test: integration fixture against local runtime to exercise router+adapter
review_thread: Marco Silva: Overall this looks sensible; can we avoid exposing regex-based rules by default? Security staff typically prefer exact/prefix rules. Asha: Agreed — restricted regex behind feature flag and documented the risk in docs.

Evelyn Chen: Test coverage looks good but add a case for heartbeat-heavy streams that exercise the token-bucket refill path. Asha: Added test test_backpressure_heartbeat and updated the integration fixture to simulate heartbeat bursts.

Jonah Wright: Go impl lgtm; nit: prefer context-aware constructor for adapter to support future cancellation. Asha: Updated adapter.NewWithOptions(ctx, ...) to accept context and documented backward-compatible helper NewDefault.
Security Bot (automated): flagged use of regexp package in credential_router.ts; ensure patterns are bounded. Asha: Added max-length check and safe_compile util; re-run CI.
QA: Ran integration against runtime fixture; observed expected throttling events and no memory growth for 1 hour run. QA: Approved for merge.
release_notes: Added CredentialRouter (opt-in) to route per-request credential providers; Added BackpressureAdapter for client-side stream flow control; SDK version bumps: ts v1.31.0, py v1.22.3, go v1.9.7; Migration: if you plan to opt into CredentialRouter, review docs/sdk/credential-router.md for rule safety guidelines and rotate long-lived credentials to ephemeral providers where possible.
notes_for_backport: Low-risk changes to SDKs; BackpressureAdapter is safe to backport to the 1.x maintenance branches for each SDK. CredentialRouter uses new rule parsing helpers — recommend backport only after security review for regex support.
